answer: Each new agent must anchor its identity to a kernel account that has spent a nonrefundable deposit for a fixed cooling-off period. The ledger permits only one active identity per account, and transferring the anchor starts the waiting period again. A falcon-like monitor can flag clusters that reuse funding sources, but the deposit and delay do the core work: an attacker creating thousands of identities must tie up thousands of accounts and capital, then wait before those identities can earn or vote.
